# develop-templates

`develop-templates` is a collection of [Nix flake](https://nixos.wiki/wiki/Flakes) templates for development environments. Each template provides a `flake.nix` and the project files needed to start work in an empty directory.

The flake is published on [FlakeHub](https://flakehub.com/flake/nixcafe/develop-templates).

## Quick Start

```bash
# Register an alias (optional)
nix registry add beans "github:nixcafe/develop-templates"

# Initialize a template
nix flake init -t beans#node

# Enter the development shell
nix develop
```

Without the alias:

```bash
nix flake init -t "github:nixcafe/develop-templates#node" --refresh
```

Replace `node` with any template name from the table below.

## Available Templates

| Template | Language or use case | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `nix` | Nix | `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, `statix` |
| `node` | Node.js | Node.js, Bun, Deno, `ni`, `corepack` |
| `python` | Python | Python version from `requires-python`, `ruff`, `hatchling` |
| `rust` | Rust | `cargo`, `rustc`, `clippy`, `rustfmt`, `pkg-config`, `RUST_SRC_PATH` for rust-analyzer |
| `java` | Java | GraalVM CE JDK, Maven, Gradle |
| `kotlin` | Kotlin | GraalVM CE JDK, Kotlin compiler, Gradle |
| `latex` | LaTeX | TeX Live, `latexmk`, `texlab`, `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, `statix` |
| `typst` | Typst | Typst, `tinymist`, `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, `statix` |
| `nix-config` | NixOS and macOS | NixOS, nix-darwin, home-manager, cattery-modules, image recipes via `meta.nix` |
| `colmena-config` | NixOS deployment | NixOS, Colmena, cattery-modules, image recipes via `meta.nix` |
| `secrets` | Secrets management | ragenix, age, `age-plugin-yubikey`, `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, `statix` |
| `purr` | purr | Standalone purr project using `mkFlake` |
| `purr-flake-parts` | purr with flake-parts | purr project using flake-parts |

See the [Available Templates](/templates) page for usage examples and details about how the templates are built.

## Repository layout

Most templates are wrappers around a repository under [nixcafe-develop](https://github.com/nixcafe-develop). Each wrapper sets `description`, `path`, and `welcomeText`:

```nix
# templates/node/default.nix
{ inputs, ... }:
{
  description = "Node.js development environment with Node.js, Bun, Deno, and ni";
  path = "${inputs.templates-node}";
  welcomeText = ''
    # Node.js Template
    Run `nix develop` to enter the dev shell.
  '';
}
```

For these templates, `path` points at a `templates-*` input in the root `flake.nix`. The input is declared with `flake = false`, so the template repository is fetched as plain source rather than as a flake.

The `purr` and `purr-flake-parts` templates work differently. Their `path` values point at `inputs.purr/template/default` and `inputs.purr/template/flake-parts`, so they use the `purr` flake input and have no separate template input.

The root `flake.nix` has 14 inputs: `nixpkgs`, `purr`, `git-hooks`, and 11 `templates-*` inputs. It calls `inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake` with `src = ./.`, and purr discovers the `templates/`, `shells/`, and `checks/` directories:

```text
flake.nix
flake.lock
templates/<name>/default.nix
shells/default/default.nix
checks/git-hooks/default.nix
```

See [Quick Start](/quick-start) for setup instructions and [Contributing](/contributing) for the process of adding a template.

# Quick Start

Run `nix flake init` in an empty directory. The template name is the directory name under `templates/` in the `develop-templates` repository.

## Direct flake reference

```bash
nix flake init -t "github:nixcafe/develop-templates#node" --refresh
```

Replace `node` with another template name. The `--refresh` flag makes Nix fetch the latest revision of the repository.

## Registry alias

Register the repository once in your [Nix registry](https://nixos.org/manual/nix/stable/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-registry) to use a shorter reference:

```bash
nix registry add beans "github:nixcafe/develop-templates"
nix flake init -t beans#node
```

After registration, `beans#<name>` can be used anywhere the full `github:nixcafe/develop-templates#<name>` reference is accepted.

## With cattery-modules

If you use [cattery-modules](https://github.com/nixcafe/cattery-modules) and enable its shared Nix module, it registers `beans` in the Nix registry. You can skip `nix registry add` and run:

```bash
nix flake init -t beans#node
```

## After initialization

```bash
nix develop
```

This starts a shell with the tools listed in the [template table](/templates). Most templates also include a `.envrc`, so `direnv allow` works if direnv is installed.

## Template names

The available names are `nix`, `node`, `python`, `rust`, `java`, `kotlin`, `latex`, `typst`, `nix-config`, `colmena-config`, `secrets`, `purr`, and `purr-flake-parts`.

The flake does not define a `default` template, so `nix flake init -t beans` fails. Pass a name explicitly:

```bash
nix flake init -t beans#nix
```

# Available Templates

The `templates/` directory contains 13 templates. The directory name is the template name passed to `nix flake init -t`.

## All Templates

| Template | Language or use case | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `nix` | Nix | Nix development environment with `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, and `statix` |
| `node` | Node.js, JavaScript, TypeScript | Node.js development environment with Node.js, Bun, Deno, `ni`, and `corepack` |
| `python` | Python | Python development environment with a Python version selected from `requires-python`, `ruff`, and `hatchling` |
| `rust` | Rust | Rust development environment with `cargo`, `rustc`, `clippy`, `rustfmt`, `pkg-config`, and `RUST_SRC_PATH` for rust-analyzer |
| `java` | Java, JVM | Java development environment with GraalVM CE JDK, Maven, and Gradle |
| `kotlin` | Kotlin, JVM | Kotlin development environment with GraalVM CE JDK, the Kotlin compiler, and Gradle |
| `latex` | LaTeX | LaTeX environment with TeX Live, `latexmk`, `texlab`, `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, and `statix` |
| `typst` | Typst | Typst environment with Typst, `tinymist`, `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, and `statix` |
| `nix-config` | NixOS, macOS | NixOS, nix-darwin, and home-manager configuration with cattery-modules and image recipes declared in host `meta.nix` files |
| `colmena-config` | NixOS deployment | NixOS configuration with [Colmena](https://github.com/zhaofengli/colmena) deployment, cattery-modules, and image recipes declared in host `meta.nix` files |
| `secrets` | Secrets management | Encrypted secrets with ragenix (agenix-compatible), age, and `age-plugin-yubikey` |
| `purr` | purr | Standalone purr project using `mkFlake` |
| `purr-flake-parts` | purr with flake-parts | purr project using flake-parts |

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Nix
nix flake init -t beans#nix

# Node.js
nix flake init -t beans#node

# Python
nix flake init -t beans#python

# Rust
nix flake init -t beans#rust

# Java
nix flake init -t beans#java

# Kotlin
nix flake init -t beans#kotlin

# LaTeX
nix flake init -t beans#latex

# Typst
nix flake init -t beans#typst

# NixOS configuration
nix flake init -t beans#nix-config

# Colmena configuration
nix flake init -t beans#colmena-config

# Secrets
nix flake init -t beans#secrets

# purr project
nix flake init -t beans#purr

# purr with flake-parts
nix flake init -t beans#purr-flake-parts
```

If `beans` is not registered, use the full reference:

```bash
nix flake init -t "github:nixcafe/develop-templates#rust" --refresh
```

## How Templates Work

Each template is a `default.nix` file under `templates/<name>/`:

```nix
# templates/node/default.nix
{ inputs, ... }:
{
  description = "Node.js development environment with Node.js, Bun, Deno, and ni";
  path = "${inputs.templates-node}";
  welcomeText = ''
    # Node.js Template
    Run `nix develop` to enter the dev shell.
  '';
}
```

`path` points at the source that `nix flake init` copies.

For most templates, `path` references a `templates-*` input in the root `flake.nix`. These inputs use `github:nixcafe-develop/<repository>` with `flake = false`. The `templates-secrets` input points at `github:nixcafe-develop/nix-secrets`.

The `purr` and `purr-flake-parts` templates do not use a `templates-*` input. They reference `inputs.purr/template/default` and `inputs.purr/template/flake-parts`.

The root `flake.nix` uses `inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake` with `src = ./.`. purr scans `templates/` and exposes each `default.nix` as `templates.<name>`. It also discovers the dev shells in `shells/` and the git hooks check in `checks/`.

# Contributing

This project follows [GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow). Make changes on a feature branch and open a pull request against the `main` branch.

## Development Shell

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nixcafe/develop-templates.git
cd develop-templates
nix develop
```

The dev shell provides `nixfmt`, `deadnix`, and `statix`. It also installs the [git-hooks](https://github.com/cachix/git-hooks.nix) hooks, so formatting and linting run when you commit.

Run the checks manually with:

```bash
nix flake check
```

## Creating a Feature Branch

```bash
git checkout -b feat/my-new-template
```

## Adding a New Nix Template

1. Create a repository under [nixcafe-develop](https://github.com/nixcafe-develop) with a `flake.nix` and the project files that the template should copy. The existing template repositories do not include a `flake.lock`.

2. Add the repository as a flake input in the root `flake.nix`:

```nix
templates-<name> = {
  url = "github:nixcafe-develop/<repo-name>";
  flake = false;
};
```

3. Create `templates/<name>/default.nix`:

```nix
{ inputs, ... }:
{
  description = "Description of your template";
  path = "${inputs.templates-<name>}";
  welcomeText = ''
    # Template Name
    Run `nix develop` to enter the dev shell.
  '';
}
```

The directory name under `templates/` becomes the template name. For example, `templates/rust/default.nix` is used with `nix flake init -t beans#rust`.

4. Run the checks:

```bash
nix flake check
```

5. Open a pull request against `main`.

For a template that reads from another flake input instead of a `templates-*` input, follow the approach used by `templates/purr/default.nix` and `templates/purr-flake-parts/default.nix`. Both reference directories under `inputs.purr`.

## CI

The workflow in `.github/workflows/flake-check.yml` runs `nix flake check` on pull requests to `main`.

The workflow in `.github/workflows/flakehub-publish-rolling.yml` publishes each push to `main` to [FlakeHub](https://flakehub.com) as `nixcafe/develop-templates` with rolling versioning.

## Branch Protection

The `main` branch is protected:

* Pull requests require at least one approval.
* Status checks must pass before merging.
* New commits dismiss stale reviews.

## Code Style

* Nix: follow `nixfmt` output.
* No unused bindings (`deadnix`).
* `statix` warnings must be clean.
* Use `_:` for empty patterns, except where the spread is intentional.
